title: Door/Handshake Calculation — Synthetic Homophily vs Influence Identification Test
status: archive-generated synthetic validation of the inference logic; not empirical evidence about real people or networks
purpose: Test whether the Door/Handshake temporal-network programme can distinguish genuine network influence from a false contagion signal created by homophilous edge formation and a persistent common environmental shock.

simulation_design.network: Undirected homophilous network. Each node has a continuous trait h_i; connection probability decreases with |h_i-h_j|. The realized benchmark network had mean degree about 12.
simulation_design.common_shock: AR(1) process c_t=0.8 c_(t-1)+epsilon_t with Gaussian innovations, creating temporally persistent shared exposure.
simulation_design.network_exposure: E_i(t-1)=fraction of i's neighbors active at the previous time step.
simulation_design.transition_model: logit P[y_i(t)=1] = -2 + 1.2 y_i(t-1) + 0.7 h_i + 0.9 c_t + alpha E_i(t-1).
scenarios: S0: alpha=0, no true network influence
S1: alpha=0.8, genuine incremental network influence

estimators.naive: Logistic/GLM state model using exposure E_i(t-1) and previous state y_i(t-1), while omitting the homophily-driving trait and common shock.
estimators.controlled: Same model plus h_i and c_t.
estimators.warning: This is a deliberately simple smoke test. Standard GLM p-values do not fully account for all dependence induced by a network panel and should not be treated as a finished inferential method. The primary diagnostic here is recovery/bias across repeated known-ground-truth simulations.

true_alpha_0.finding: Homophily plus the persistent common shock produced an extremely strong false contagion signal when those causes were omitted. Adding the variables that generated selection/common exposure removed the spurious influence estimate.

true_alpha_0_8.finding: When genuine influence was present, the controlled model recovered an exposure coefficient close to the true value while the naive model remained severely upward biased.

scientific_interpretation.core_result: A Handshake/contagion model can appear strongly confirmed even when true influence is exactly zero if relationship selection and common environmental drivers are not modeled.
scientific_interpretation.project_value: The model's serious contribution is therefore not the claim that relational influence exists everywhere; it is a framework for asking whether a measured network effect survives explicit selection/common-cause controls.
scientific_interpretation.door_translation: Edge formation is one Door process and state transition is another. Estimating propagation without modeling the edge-generating Door can manufacture a false influence story.
scientific_interpretation.negative_result_value: If a real-data influence coefficient collapses after better selection/common-source controls, that is a successful scientific use of the model even though the romantic 'contagion' interpretation fails.

next_validation_steps: Repeat over a much broader grid of homophily strength, common-shock persistence, network density and true alpha.
Use cluster/network-robust uncertainty or a model whose likelihood explicitly represents node/time dependence.
Fit the edge-formation and state-transition processes jointly rather than treating the generated network as fixed.
Add unobserved confounding to measure how badly the controlled model degrades when the common cause is not directly measurable.
Test intervention/natural-experiment estimators where a causal interpretation is intended.
Only after synthetic calibration, choose a real temporal dataset with independently defined states and edge events.
failure_conditions: The joint/controlled model cannot recover known alpha across reasonable synthetic regimes.
Small changes in network density/time resolution reverse the inferred sign or magnitude without a modeled reason.
Real applications lack variables or design information capable of distinguishing common exposure from interpersonal influence.
Project labels such as Life/Strife cannot be coded with adequate reliability.

external_context.use: Documents the same core identification problem: observed similarity can arise from contagion, homophily or common social/environmental factors.
